what: Leaf shadows, as if cast by a tree outside the window, multiply over the panel (text and photos too) and sway in the wind — a crisp leaf layer (opacity .75) and a large blurred lower layer (.51) are lit by two projectors, and the leaf-grain coordinates ripple with branch sines (vertical 22, horizontal 11) and leaf sines (83, −57) (gust .72 ± .18·.1 rising and falling at .37·.61 Hz). The two layers drift by 2.6% and 1.6% of screen width × sway following sin(.7t)·sin(.43t) and rotate by sin(.31t) × .01 rad. Time runs at per-second speed × 2.4. Moving the mouse pushes them shift px opposite the cursor with .85s power3.out, giving the same parallax as the 3D scene.

options.soft: Opacity of the lower smudge layer, default .51
options.shift: Cursor parallax (px, at the screen edge), default 0 — off
options.from: Side where leaves gather — branches grow only to the right of this value within 0~.9 of the canvas width, default 0 (even)
options.x · y · size · angle: Center (panel ratio), size (long-side multiple) and angle (rad) of the crisp layered spotlight, default .8 · .32 · 1.3 · −.341
options.mx · my: Center of the layered spotlight that stays clear below panel width 768px, default x · y as is — for pushing the leaves to one end on phones
options.res: Render resolution scale, default .5 (half resolution is enough for a blurred shadow)

note: Shadow color is --fx-shade (default color-mix(--kf-ink 72%, --kf-bg)) — it is multiply, so the brighter the background, the fainter the shadow. The original projected a leaf photo (gobo) onto the floor and cards with WGSL, here the leaf pattern is redrawn on a canvas and laid over the whole page in a single WebGL layer (looks the same for a top-down scene). When the background changes, fx:theme is sent to re-read the color. With reduced motion, only one frame is drawn
